metadata.title: IEA International Civic and Citizenship Education Study 2022 Assessment Framework

survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: This document is an assessment framework for ICCS 2022 rather than an empirical analysis paper. It describes the study’s conceptual background, constructs, and assessment design (including paper-based and computer-based delivery options), but it does not report an analytic dataset, sampling weights, or replicate-weight procedures. As a result, no specific weight variable (e.g., student sampling weights or BRR/jackknife replicate weights) can be extracted from the text provided. For secondary analyses using ICCS 2022 microdata, analysts should apply the official ICCS sampling weights and replicate weights supplied with the international database to account for the complex multistage design and nested data structure (students within schools within countries).

data.handling_not_reported_explanation: This is a framework/assessment-design publication that specifies what ICCS 2022 intends to measure (civic knowledge, civic attitudes and engagement, and contextual factors) and how instruments are structured. It does not present student-level predictive models or any analysis of cognitive achievement scores that would require plausible values (PV) handling. Missing-data handling is also not applicable here because the document does not run an empirical estimation procedure on an analytic sample.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: Used as an assessment framework for ICCS 2022; the document provided does not report an analytic student sample or any inclusion/exclusion criteria for an empirical dataset.

data.outcome_summary: ICCS 2022 is the third cycle in its current form and the fifth IEA study of civic and citizenship education, designed to measure students’ civic knowledge and their civic attitudes and engagement, alongside contextual information from students, teachers, schools, and national contexts surveys. The framework specifies four parts: a civic knowledge framework (cognitive content and processes), a civic attitudes and engagement framework (affective-behavioral constructs), a contextual framework (multi-level context variables), and an assessment design chapter detailing instrument coverage, item types, and the described achievement scale. A key implementation feature is the option of computer-based delivery for the student survey (with about two-thirds of participating countries choosing it), including computer-enhanced modules that simulate participatory real-world scenarios with interactive feedback. The framework also emphasizes comparability across paper and computer modes and across cycles (2009, 2016, 2022), while broadening content to sustainability, digital civic engagement, diversity, young people’s views of the political system, and global citizenship.
data.null_fields_interpretation: This publication is an assessment framework rather than an empirical study estimating effects or training predictive models. Consequently, there is no reported analytic sample size, no country-level sample breakdown, no PV or missing-data handling strategy for an estimation model, and no ML algorithm evaluation. The extraction therefore focuses on the study design and measurement scope described in the framework, with main_findings left empty because no predictive outcomes or performance metrics are reported.
